questions.question: How does Theorem 1.1 refine eventual linearity of regularity for powers?

options.A: For each local-cohomology index i, the normalized end degree has a limit, and for some i it is at least indeg(M)
options.B: Every individual ai(t) is eventually linear, with a common constant term
options.C: The regularity is eventually constant and equals the initial degree of I
options.D: The normalized limit exists only for i=0 and equals −∞

questions.rationale: The theorem asserts existence of the normalized limit for any i and a lower bound by indeg(M) for at least one i.

questions.question: What does Theorem 1.1's integer d measure in terms of the ideal and module?

options.A: The least degree cutoff μ for which I≤μ stabilizes the action on some power IpM
options.B: The Krull dimension of A/I, independent of M
options.C: The largest degree of a minimal generator of M
options.D: The least cohomological index with nonzero local cohomology

questions.rationale: The definition takes a minimum over μ such that (I≤μ)IpM=Ip+1M for some p.

questions.question: What caveat do Cutkosky's examples establish about the theorem's limit statement?

options.A: The limit result does not imply every ai(t) is eventually linear; at least one is
options.B: The limits fail to exist whenever ai(t) oscillates at finite t
options.C: All local-cohomology functions are eventually periodic rather than linear
options.D: The leading slope can change with i, so no normalized limit can be compared

questions.rationale: The introduction explicitly notes that the limit result only forces at least one function to be eventually linear.
questions.evidence_quote: It only implies that at least one of them is eventually linear in t.

questions.question: What geometric condition characterizes a nonnegative finite limit for the normalized regularity of saturated powers?

options.A: The graph projection π has a positive-dimensional fiber
options.B: The projection π is finite and every fiber is reduced
options.C: The ideal has analytic spread exactly one
options.D: Every fiber has dimension zero but nonconstant Hilbert polynomial

questions.rationale: Corollary 1.2 equates a nonnegative/not −∞ limit with existence of a positive-dimensional fiber.
questions.evidence_quote: admits a ﬁber of positive dimension.

options.B: Any projective morphism with positive-dimensional fibers
options.C: Finite morphisms between reduced schemes of equal dimension
options.D: Flat morphisms whose source is a standard graded domain
